Strait of Hormuz Status: October 11, 2026 | Straits Daily Brief
Skip to content Straits Hormuz Live Monitor Day  225 Open? Live map News About Method API Live

Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
11 October 2026 .
Brent $ 104.72 + 0.42 % · Transits 4 (2026-10-04) · AI-assisted
01 gCaptain reports more tankers were hit in the Strait of Hormuz as US forces struck a cargo ship in the Gulf of Oman.

02 Per Iranian state media, relayed by Reuters, Iran says the US response to its proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz was insufficient.

03 IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on October 4, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains closed to commercial traffic, with vessel damage and military strikes continuing into the current window. gCaptain reports that additional tankers were hit in the strait while US forces struck a cargo ship in the Gulf of Oman; Al Jazeera separately reports that CENTCOM said it disabled a vessel attempting to run the blockade. Iranian state media, relayed by Reuters, say the US response to Iran's proposal for reopening the strait was insufficient, though the terms of the US reply have not been published; the claim originates with Iranian authorities and is not independent corroboration. NewsCord and CNN carry the IRGC's assertion that an oil supertanker exploded after striking a mine on an unauthorized route, a claim originating with Iranian state media that no maritime authority has confirmed. gCaptain and The Times of Israel report a tanker was damaged after being struck in the strait. IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on October 4, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. Brent settled at $104.72 at Friday's close, up 0.42% on the session; futures are shut. The 54 headlines indexed in the past 24 hours reflect continued high activity across the diplomatic and maritime tracks, with no resolution to the standoff between US conditions and Iran's seven-point reopening plan. As of 18:20 UTC, 119 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, flat over 24 hours, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the high band, flat over 24 hours, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
